name: Multi-Agent Orchestrator
tag: Configure a team of AI agents, simulate the pipeline, then run it on real work.

scenarios.title: Process supplier onboarding forms
scenarios.ask: Set up a pipeline for {forms} supplier onboarding forms a week with {agents} agents and a {check} check.
steps: Built a {agents}-agent pipeline: Reader, Validator, Risk scorer{=0 * agents} and Filer, with roles and handoff rules.
Ran 25 sample forms. {=25 - 3} passed, 3 stopped at the Validator for a missing tax ID.
Adjusted the Risk scorer so new suppliers in high-risk categories always go to a person.
Switched to live mode for {forms} forms a week with a {check} at the end.
followups: It lets you see how forms flow, where they stop and what each agent decides, before any real supplier data is touched.
Can we add an agent later?
Yes. Drag a new agent into the pipeline, set its handoff rule and re-run the simulation before going live.

scenarios.title: Draft a weekly market brief
scenarios.ask: Have a Researcher, Analyst and Editor produce a weekly brief from {feeds} news feeds, in {words} words.
steps: Read about {=feeds * 25} articles from {feeds} feeds and kept {=min(30, feeds * 3)} relevant ones.
Grouped them into {=min(6, max(2, round(feeds / 4)))} themes and noted what changed since last week.
Wrote a {words}-word brief and cut repeated points.
Checked every claim links to an article before publishing to the team channel.
followups: Can each agent use a different model?
Yes. A common setup uses a fast model for the Researcher and a stronger one for the Editor.
What if a feed goes down?
The Orchestrator notes the missing feed in the brief and runs with the rest.

scenarios.title: Handle a spike in returns
scenarios.ask: Returns jumped to {returns} a day after a sale. Run the returns pipeline with {agents} parallel lanes.
steps: Read return requests and photos and sorted them by reason.
Sent {=round(returns * 0.2)} unusual cases, such as missing order numbers, to the support team.
Balanced work across {agents} lanes. Queue clears in about {=ceil(returns * 0.5 / agents / 60)} hours.
followups: You do. The Policy agent can auto-approve only under a dollar limit you choose. Above it, a person signs off.
Can lanes scale on their own?
Yes. Set a target queue time and the Orchestrator adds lanes up to your cap when the queue grows.
